Gold/Silver Ratio

This ratio shows how many ounces of silver are equivalent to one ounce of gold. It is calculated by dividing the daily gold closing price by the silver closing price on the same calendar date.

Calculating the Gold/Silver ratio…

Why investors watch this ratio

A rising Gold/Silver ratio means gold is strengthening relative to silver. A falling ratio means silver is strengthening relative to gold.

The ratio can provide historical and market context, but a high or low value does not guarantee that prices will reverse.

Historical context and typical ranges

The gold/silver ratio has a long history as one of the oldest tracked financial metrics. For most of the twentieth century, the ratio traded in a broad range between roughly 40 and 80. During the COVID-19 shock of March 2020, silver collapsed far faster than gold and the ratio briefly touched 125 — the highest level in modern history. It then compressed sharply as silver recovered, falling back below 70 within a year.

In 2026, with gold trading near all-time highs above $3,000 per ounce and silver lagging, the ratio has spent much of the year elevated above 85. Historically, sustained periods above 80 have eventually been followed by periods of silver outperformance, though the timing is unpredictable.

What a high or low ratio means in practice

A high ratio — gold expensive relative to silver — can reflect a few different things: a flight to safety where gold is bought as a monetary hedge while silver, with its industrial demand component, lags; a risk-off environment where manufacturing and industrial outlook is weakening; or simply a period where investment demand for gold has outrun investment demand for silver.

A low ratio — silver expensive relative to gold — typically coincides with strong industrial growth, commodity bull markets, and periods when investors are rotating from gold into more cyclical assets. The ratio tends to compress fastest during commodity supercycles or periods of aggressive industrial expansion.

How GoldAlert calculates this ratio

GoldAlert divides the daily closing price of gold (XAU/USD) by the daily closing price of silver (XAG/USD) using the same calendar date for both inputs. Both prices come from the same daily data feed, eliminating any bid-ask or timing discrepancy between the two metals. The result is displayed as a single number — for example, a ratio of 90 means one troy ounce of gold buys 90 troy ounces of silver at current close prices.

The chart on this page shows the ratio over time, so you can see whether the current reading is historically high, low, or within the middle of its recent range. A direction indicator shows whether the ratio has moved higher or lower over the past session.
